name: Spacecore

influenced_by: early-2010s galaxy-print leggings as a specific retail fashion trend

reacts_against: nothing specific; spacecore grew from a genuine, widely shared fascination with deep-space imagery becoming newly accessible through NASA's expanding public photo archives in the 2010s.
article: Spacecore's rise through early-2010s Tumblr tracks closely with a specific, dateable retail moment: galaxy-print leggings, printed with deep-space nebula photography, became a genuine mass-market fashion trend around 2012–13, selling widely enough that the print briefly became a recognizable shorthand for internet-native style on its own. The aesthetic drew its visual material directly from NASA's increasingly accessible public photography archives — the same Hubble Space Telescope images circulating as desktop wallpapers and screensavers fed straight into fashion print design. Spacecore's palette (deep cosmic purple-black, metallic silver, scattered pinpoint light) differs from most of this archive's other aesthetics in having a literal, traceable photographic source rather than growing out of a subculture's clothing or a design movement's furniture — it's closer in spirit to how vaporwave borrowed specific found imagery than to how, say, grunge grew out of a music scene's practical dress.

findings: dark — about 65% of the measured color across 6 wiki images is below mid-lightness
a vivid streak — roughly 32% of the color measured is highly saturated
mostly muted — about 54% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
measured.caveat: Colors measured from Aesthetics Wiki images as photographed and displayed on screen; actual materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
